sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the instant complaint case was filed due to matrimonial dispute between applicant no. 1 and opposite party no. 3, however, the complaint was filed by the opposite party no. 2 who is the father of the opposite party no. 3.

The aforesaid matrimonial dispute between the parties was amicably settled and an application u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act was filed wherein the settlement between the parties was recorded in the said petition itself.

In paragraph no. 5 which reads as under:-
"5. That the parties to this petition have decided/ settled all their disputes relating to this marriage and the controversies in regard to dowry/Istridhan articles, past,
present and future maintenance.

Both the petitioners have dissolved their marriage by way Compromise Deed dated 20.02.2018, terms conditions and Compromise Deed as under:- of the of the said Compromise Deed as under :-
(i) That both the parties have resolved their disputes/claims amicably in respect of this marriage for obtaining divorce by mutual consent from the Matrimonial Court.
(ii) That the petitioner No. 2 will withdraw all the cases filed by himself and on behalf of himself against the petitioner no. 1 and her family members.

The petitioner no.
1will also withdraw all the cases filed by herself and on behalf of herself against the petitioner no. 2 and his family members.

(iii) That the petitionerno. her 1 has already received her entire Jewellery and personal belongings including valuable clothes from the petitioner no. 2 in the presence of her parents and the petitioner no. 1 has returned the items of the petitioner no. 2.

(iv) That the petitioner no. 1 has setcled all her remaining claims of marriage,
expenses and maintenance (present, past and future) and all other claims in respect of this marriage with the petitioner no. 2.

(v) That both the petitioner no. 1 & petitioner no. 2 undertake not to file any kind of case i.e. Civil, Criminal and Matrimonial, and complaints before any Court of law,
Police or public authority in any part of India against each other.
(vi) That both the parties undertake to file a joint petition for Divorce by mutual consent of under Section 13 (B) (1) of Hindu Marriage Act before the concerned Matrimonial Court and shall appear before the Matrimonial Court for recording of their statements along with their counsel.

(vii) That the petitioner no. 1 undertakes to co-operate with the petitioner no. 2 in getting the FIRs quashed from the competant Court of law and to sign and execute any kind of documents and to appear and give statement in the Court of law in this regard.

2 (viii) That the petitioners undertake to file the Second Motion of divorce petition under Section 13(B) (2) of H.M. Act within a week after the expiry of the stipulated period after recording of statement in the first motion of divorce petition under Section 13(B) (1) of H.M. Act."

sentences.text: 4. In terms of the aforesaid settlement, an application u/s 13-B was filed which was ultimately decreed by the trial court in presence of the parties and the marriage between the applicant no. 1 and opposite party no. 3 was dissolved vide order dated 10.05.2018, therefore, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceedings of the instant case.
5. In the instant application vide order dated 15.03.2019, initially the notice was issued to the opposite party no. 2.

The notice was duly served as per the office report dated 09.08.2020, despite service of notice, there is no appearance on behalf of the opposite party no. 2, therefore, it is presumed that the opposite party no. 2 and 3 have no objection with regard to the quashing of the proceeding of the instant complaint case.
6. In view of the settlement which has been arrived at between the parties which has been recorded in the application u/s 13-B filed by the applicant no. 1 and the opposite party no. 3 jointly.

7. In view thereof, since the instant proceedings are arising out of matrimonial dispute which has already been settled and the decree of dissolution of marriage has already been passed by mutual consent dissolving the marriage between the applicant no. 1 and opposite party no. 3 and the parties has already agreed to withdraw the cases filed by them against each other.
8.

In view thereof, no fruitful purpose would be served by keeping the instant criminal proceedings pending against the applicant and the aforesaid settlement has already been verified by the trial court while passing the decree of dissolution of marriage u/s 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act.

9. In view thereof, the instant application is allowed and the entire proceedings ofComplaint Case No. 187 of 2018 (Arvind Porwal Vs. Atul Kumar and others) U/s 498A, 506 IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act,
P.S. Dibiyapur, District Auraiya, pending in the court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate,
Auraiya
